findings.title: Most operators lack REGISTER and UNDO bl_options
findings.description: Of 17 operator classes, only FLUIDSIM_OT_initialize (REGISTER only), FLUIDSIM_OT_setup_scene (REGISTER+UNDO), and FLUIDSIM_OT_tag_object (REGISTER+UNDO) specify bl_options. The remaining 14 operators have no bl_options at all: release, reset, step, toggle_live, inject_particles, run_validation, run_benchmark, write_report, snippet_add, snippet_remove, snippet_argument_add, snippet_argument_remove, snippet_apply, export_frame. Without REGISTER, operators may not appear in the UI menu search or respond to keymaps. Without UNDO, users cannot revert scene-modifying operations like inject_particles, reset, or snippet_add/remove.
findings.impact: Users cannot undo destructive operations (reset, particle injection, snippet removal). Operators cannot be invoked via search or keymap binding. Relies entirely on panel button invocation.
findings.fix: Add bl_options = {"REGISTER", "UNDO"} to operators that modify scene state (reset, inject_particles, snippet_add/remove/argument_add/argument_remove). Add bl_options = {"REGISTER"} to all other operators at minimum.

findings.title: FLUIDSIM_OT_export_frame cannot show file browser without invoke method
findings.description: FLUIDSIM_OT_export_frame defines a `filepath` StringProperty with subtype FILE_PATH but has no `invoke()` method to call the file browser (context.window_manager.fileselect_add). The filepath defaults to '//fluidsim_frame' and is used directly in execute(). Users must manually type a path in the properties panel, which is non-standard for Blender export operators and will confuse users expecting a Save As dialog.
findings.impact: Export operator is nearly unusable via the UI. Users cannot browse to select an export location. The filepath stored in the property may be relative to an unexpected directory.
findings.fix: Add an invoke() method that calls context.window_manager.fileselect_add(self) to show the file browser. Set bl_options to include {'REGISTER'} and override draw() or use default file browser behavior.

findings.title: Frame change handler suppresses all exceptions silently during playback
findings.description: The _on_frame_change handler (line 458-463) catches all exceptions with a bare except clause and only sets sess.error + prints to console. Users watching the viewport see no visual error indicator — the simulation simply stops updating or produces wrong results. Error state is only visible if the overlay is enabled and shown, and even then it's a single line 'error: ...' text in a dense overlay.
findings.impact: Critical simulation errors during playback are invisible to users. A solver crash looks identical to a pause. Users cannot tell if the simulation is running correctly or has failed silently.
findings.fix: Add a dedicated error box or status indicator in the Simulation panel that becomes prominent (e.g., red background) when sess.error is non-empty. Consider re-raising in debug builds or adding a notification operator.

findings.title: Overlay draw handler reads bpy.context directly, causing crash risk
findings.description: The _draw_overlay function (line 366) uses `bpy.context` directly — a global reference that can be None or stale when invoked from certain viewport states (e.g., background rendering, script context switches, or during Blender shutdown). The handler also does not validate context.scene.fluidsim existence before accessing it (line 369). This can cause AttributeError or RuntimeError crashes that bring down the entire viewport.
findings.impact: Viewport overlay can crash Blender if context is unavailable or during edge states. The draw handler is registered globally and runs in the render thread without context safety guarantees.
findings.fix: Wrap the entire draw body in a try/except that silently returns on error. Use context_override or pass the region context explicitly. Guard all property accesses with hasattr/getattr checks.

findings.title: Validation and benchmark operators run synchronously with no progress feedback
findings.description: FLUIDSIM_OT_run_validation (line 245) and FLUIDSIM_OT_run_benchmark (line 273) execute long-running GPU operations (~30s for validation, variable for benchmarks) synchronously in the execute() method. Neither calls context.window_manager.progress_begin/update/end to show progress. The UI thread blocks completely, making Blender appear frozen. The benchmark's progress callback parameter is never used by the Blender operator.
findings.impact: Users see a frozen UI for 30+ seconds with no feedback. New users may force-quit Blender thinking it has crashed. Advanced users cannot gauge remaining time.
findings.fix: Use a modal operator pattern or Blender's built-in progress bar (context.window_manager.progress_begin/update/end). Pass a progress callback to run_all() and run_benchmark() that updates the progress bar. Consider running on a background thread with operator polling.

findings.title: Source panel shows emission settings for sink and force roles
findings.description: FLUIDSIM_PT_sources (line 150-170) draws a settings box for the active object if its role is SOURCE, SINK, or FORCE, but the content unconditionally shows source-specific properties: emit_rate, initial_velocity, use_object_velocity, temperature, viscosity, use_lifespan. For SINK and FORCE roles, these fields are irrelevant or confusing (e.g., a Force region showing 'Emit Rate' and 'Temperature').
findings.impact: Users tagging a sink or force object see misleading source properties. Can cause confusion about what settings actually apply to the simulation.
findings.fix: Gate the source-specific fields behind `if pg.role == 'SOURCE':` and show sink-specific or force-specific fields for the other roles. Provide role-appropriate field labels or a brief explanation.

findings.title: Colliders panel has no per-object sink settings section
findings.description: FLUIDSIM_PT_colliders allows tagging objects as SINK (line 206) but shows no settings for sink properties when a sink object is selected. The panel only shows collider-specific settings (friction, restitution, transfer_velocity). Sinks created via Tag Sink have no configurable options in the UI beyond what the domain-level height source provides.
findings.impact: Users who tag sinks have no way to configure sink behavior (suck speed, activation radius, etc.) through the panel. The sink feature appears broken or incomplete.
findings.fix: Add a dedicated sink settings section (similar to collider section at lines 209-218) that displays when context.active_object.fluidsim.role == 'SINK'.

findings.title: Snippet argument remove operator has no UI indicator which argument is removed
findings.description: FLUIDSIM_OT_snippet_argument_remove (operators.py line 397) always removes the last argument from the active snippet's arguments list, with no visual indicator of which argument will be removed. The UI only shows 'Remove Arg' button. If a user has reordered or added multiple arguments, they cannot target a specific argument for removal.
findings.impact: Users cannot remove arbitrary arguments from the middle of the list. Removing arguments is destructive and unpredictable without visual feedback.
findings.fix: Add an index-based remove (one remove button per argument row, passing the index) or add a 'Remove' button next to each argument row that calls remove on that specific index. Update the operator to accept an argument_index parameter.

findings.title: Snippet last_error is truncated to 64 characters, losing diagnostic information
findings.description: The snippet error display (line 405) truncates snip.last_error to 64 characters via string slicing [:64]. Warp/CUDA compilation errors often contain file paths, line numbers, and column hints that exceed 64 characters. A 64-character truncation loses virtually all actionable diagnostic information, making kernel debugging impossible.
findings.impact: Users cannot debug custom Warp snippet compilation errors. Error messages like 'File line 42: syntax error near ...' are cut off before the useful part.
findings.fix: Increase truncation to 256 or 512 characters, or use a multi-line label with word wrap. Consider adding a 'Show Full Error' operator that copies the error to clipboard or opens a text block. Use a sub-panel expandable section for error details.

findings.title: Broad exception handlers produce technical error messages unfriendly to users
findings.description: Many operators catch `Exception as exc` and report `f'Solver initialization failed: {exc}'` or similar, passing the raw Python exception repr (or str()) to the user interface. These messages can include CUDA driver errors, memory address traces, or Warp internal backtraces that are meaningless to non-developer users. The same pattern appears in initialize (line 28), step (line 89), toggle_live (line 110), run_validation (line 258), run_benchmark (line 292), and the frame handler (scene_bridge.py line 460).
findings.impact: Users see cryptic technical error messages. Cannot distinguish between 'fixable' errors (e.g., 'out of memory') and 'fatal' errors. May report bugs that are actually configuration issues.
findings.fix: Map known exception types to user-friendly messages (e.g., CUDA OOM -> 'GPU out of memory, try reducing max particles or voxel count'). Preserve full exception text in the status property for advanced users, but display a simplified message in the operator report.

findings.title: Validation operator hardcodes 'cuda:0' device ignoring user preference
findings.description: FLUIDSIM_OT_run_validation.execute calls `validation.run_all(device='cuda:0')` on line 257, ignoring the user's device selection in the addon preferences (preferences.py line 26). Users who have configured a different CUDA device will run validation on the wrong GPU.
findings.impact: Validation runs on potentially wrong GPU device. On systems with multiple GPUs or where 'cuda:0' is not the intended device, results may be misleading or tests may fail for device-specific reasons.
findings.fix: Read the device from addon preferences: `prefs = bpy.context.preferences.addons['fluidSim_warp_blender51'].preferences; device = prefs.device`. Same pattern used in scene_bridge.py line 81-83 for settings; reuse that pattern.

findings.title: Device preference is a free-form string instead of an enumerated list
findings.description: The `device` StringProperty (line 26) allows any arbitrary text input. Users must know to type 'cuda:0', 'cuda:1', etc. There is no validation or dropdown of available CUDA devices. The _probe_warp function checks CUDA availability but does not enumerate specific devices. Mistyping silently falls through to Warp's default device behavior.
findings.impact: Users may enter an invalid or mistyped device identifier and receive no immediate feedback. Cannot discover available devices without consulting system tools.
findings.fix: Use an EnumProperty populated at registration time by probing available Warp devices via `wp.get_cuda_devices()` or similar. Provide a 'Detect Devices' button that refreshes the list. Fall back to 'cuda:0' with a warning if probing fails.

findings.title: Global module-level SESSION object prevents multi-scene simulation workflows
findings.description: The _SESSION variable (line 39) is a module-level singleton shared across all scenes. If a user switches to a different scene in Blender, the session still points to the original scene's solver context. Scene properties (domain, sources) are re-read during sync_scene_to_solver, but the solver state, frame count, and profile data remain from the original scene. This can cause cross-scene contamination.
findings.impact: Users working with multiple scenes will experience state leakage: changing scenes does not switch simulation contexts. An initialized solver in scene A persists when switching to scene B.
findings.fix: Make session per-scene (keyed by scene UUID/name) or detect scene changes and auto-switch. At minimum, add a warning in the status bar or panel when the active scene's settings don't match the session's stored scene reference.

findings.title: release_session leaves stale validation and benchmark data in session
findings.description: release_session (line 369-375) sets solver and profiler to None and clears frame_stats and _collider_prev, but leaves validation_results, benchmark_result, benchmark_compare, and error fields intact. If a user re-initializes the solver after releasing, old validation/benchmark data persists and is shown in the UI as if it belongs to the new solver session.
findings.impact: Stale benchmark comparisons and validation results are displayed after solver re-initialization. Users may compare a new solver state against old benchmark data from a different configuration.
findings.fix: Clear sess.validation_results, sess.benchmark_result, sess.benchmark_compare, and sess.error in release_session(), alongside the other fields.

findings.title: Viewport output objects are recreated every frame causing flickering
findings.description: update_outputs calls _swap_mesh and _swap_points which create new Blender datablocks (bpy.data.meshes.new, bpy.data.pointclouds.new) every frame and replace the object's data pointer. Old datablocks are deleted if orphaned. This rapid create/destroy cycle causes viewport flickering in wireframe and solid views, increases memory allocation pressure, and is not undo-safe — the Blender depsgraph registers each datablock creation as a potential undo step.
findings.impact: Viewport flickers during simulation playback as meshes are swapped each frame. Memory fragmentation from repeated alloc/free cycles. Potential undo stack bloat on long simulations.
findings.fix: Reuse existing mesh/pointcloud datablocks by directly overwriting vertex/point data in-place (BMIter for mesh editing, or foreach_set on existing attributes) instead of creating new datablocks. Use mesh.clear() followed by from_pydata() or similar in-place update methods.

findings.title: Imports executed inside draw methods on every redraw
findings.description: FLUIDSIM_PT_simulation imports `from .blender.scene_bridge import session` inside draw() (line 28-29). FLUIDSIM_PT_domain imports `from .blender.scene_bridge import _domain_bounds, session` inside draw() (line 88-89). FLUIDSIM_PT_diagnostics similarly imports inside draw() (line 416-417). While Python caches module imports, the name binding happens on every panel redraw (multiple times per frame during playback), adding measurable overhead.
findings.impact: Minor performance degradation during viewport interaction. Panel redraws are frequent during simulation playback with profiler timers updating.
findings.fix: Move all imports to the top of the module (or at least to module level), or import the scene_bridge module once at class level. Python's import cache means the cost is in attribute lookup, not file I/O, but repeated attribute lookups in hot paths add up.

findings.title: Timer name mapping duplicated between panels.py and viewport.py
findings.description: The phase name-to-label mapping for profiler timers is defined independently in FLUIDSIM_PT_diagnostics.draw() (panels.py lines 431-439) and _draw_overlay() (viewport.py lines 394-400). The two mappings have slight differences: panels.py omits 'compute_7' (advection) and 'compute_9' (sink) and names 'compute_15' as 'Topology' while viewport.py names it 'misc'. Any update to timer phases must be made in two places, creating a maintenance burden and risk of stale mappings.
findings.impact: Panel and overlay displays may show different timer names for the same phase. Adding or renaming phases requires updating two files or the displays diverge silently.
findings.fix: Define the phase-to-label mapping once (e.g., in sim/constants.py or a shared utility module) and import it in both panels.py and viewport.py. Eliminate the duplicate definitions.

findings.title: Viewport overlay text density makes information hard to parse at a glance
findings.description: The overlay line 2 (lines 388-390) concatenates particle count, whitewater count, voxel count, substeps, and timing into a single line without visual separation: 'particles 123,456   whitewater 789   voxels 12,345   substeps 3   4.2 ms/frame'. The timer breakdown (when enabled) appends more data in a single line with tab-like spaces. Users scanning the viewport during simulation cannot quickly find the specific metric they need.
findings.impact: Reduced usability of the overlay for real-time monitoring. Users must visually parse dense text to find individual metrics.
findings.fix: Break the overlay into multiple lines (one per metric group: particles, performance, timers). Use consistent spacing and consider color-coding or labels. Each metric block should be visually distinct.

findings.title: Forces panel header text says 'Source' but force role exists separately
findings.description: FLUIDSIM_PT_forces.draw() displays 'Per-object force regions (tag as Source):' (line 240). However, there is a dedicated 'FORCE' role that can be assigned via FLUIDSIM_OT_tag_object (operators.py line 191-193) which does not include a FORCE tag option. The instruction tells users to tag as Source, but source objects have their own emission-focused panel. Users may be confused about whether to use SOURCE role or a separate mechanism.
findings.impact: Users may not discover the force feature properly. The instruction to 'tag as Source' is misleading since the panel also checks for role 'FORCE' but there is no way to tag an object as FORCE through the UI operators.
findings.fix: Either add a 'Tag Force' button to the Forces panel that sets role to FORCE, or update the role options in FLUIDSIM_OT_tag_object to include 'FORCE'. Update the panel instruction text to match the actual workflow.

findings.title: Domain resolution display uses division by voxel_size without zero guard
findings.description: Line 92 computes resolution as `int(d / max(fs.voxel_size, 1e-6))`, clamping voxel_size away from zero for the division. However, if voxel_size is set to an extremely small value (below 0.005 which is the current min property bound), the displayed resolution could exceed reasonable display limits and overflow the integer. The min property bound is 0.005 but this clamp covers programming errors.
findings.impact: Primarily a defensive coding concern. If a user managed to set voxel_size below the property min bound (e.g., via script), the displayed resolution value could overflow or display nonsensical numbers.
findings.fix: Consider formatting the resolution display with a human-readable suffix (e.g., '2.1M' for millions) and clamp the display value to prevent overflow. This is a minor display polish issue.

findings.title: FLUIDSIM_OT_step silently auto-initializes solver as a side effect
findings.description: FLUIDSIM_OT_step.execute() (line 80-83) automatically calls bridge.initialize_session(scene) if the solver is not active, before executing the step. This side effect is not signaled to the user — the operator button text and the panel live state do not change. Users who click 'Step 1' or 'Step 10' may unexpectedly trigger a full solver reinitialization, discarding any existing manual configuration.
findings.impact: Users may accidentally reinitialize the solver by clicking 'Step' when the solver was released or never initialized. A long initialization delay may appear unexpectedly. Any pending changes that were not explicitly synced are applied during reinit.
findings.fix: Instead of auto-initializing, show a descriptive error message ('Solver not initialized - use Initialize Solver first') and return CANCELLED. Alternatively, use a confirmation dialog via the invoke() method to warn users before auto-initializing.

findings.title: Tag Clear resets display and render properties as hidden side effects
findings.description: FLUIDSIM_OT_tag_object with role='NONE' (line 211-213) resets obj.display_type to 'TEXTURED' and obj.hide_render to False. These side effects are unrelated to the simulation role and modify the user's viewport/render settings without warning. An object originally set to 'WIRE' display or with hide_render=True will have those preferences silently overwritten.
findings.impact: User viewport preferences on cleared objects are overwritten. Objects that were intentionally hidden from render become visible when their simulation role is cleared.
findings.fix: Only set obj.fluidsim.role = 'NONE' and leave display_type and hide_render unchanged. If restoring defaults is desired, store the original values when tagging (e.g., in custom properties) and restore them on clear.

findings.title: Toggle Live operator button icon logic decoupled from actual state
findings.description: FLUIDSIM_OT_toggle_live sets fs.live = True or False (lines 113, 116) and the panel draw method (panels.py line 40-42) chooses icon/text based on fs.live. However, the operator bl_label 'Toggle Live Simulation' and the context from which it is called are the only references. If fs.live is changed externally (e.g., by another operator or reset), the toggle button may display inconsistent state until pressed.
findings.impact: Minor UI inconsistency if the live state is modified outside of the toggle operator. The button may show 'Live: On' when the solver is not actually stepping during playback.
findings.fix: The panel already checks `fs.live` for display (line 40-42), which is correct. Ensure that any code path that changes live state (reset, release) also resets fs.live to False. Currently, release_session() does not touch fs.live, which could leave it True after solver is released.

findings.title: Suppressed exceptions during frame stepping may mask cache failures from user
findings.description: step_frame() (line 415) silently catches cache write failures with `except Exception as exc: print(...)`. While this is intentional (cache is supplemental), users with cache_enabled=True may believe data is being written to disk when it is silently failing. The console print is invisible to typical users.
findings.impact: Users who enable caching may assume frames are being saved when they are not. Silent failures mean corrupted or missing cache data goes undetected until the user tries to restore from cache.
findings.fix: Report cache failures through the status string or a warning report. At minimum, set `fs.status = 'Cache write failed'` or provide a tooltip/icon next to the cache_enabled checkbox when errors have occurred.

findings.title: Benchmark comparison result string not enumerated for display
findings.description: The benchmark comparison result (line 483) displays `sess.benchmark_compare['result']` directly. If the result string changes in the comparison module (e.g., from 'pass' to 'performance_regression'), the panel will show the raw string, which may not be user-friendly without explanation of what it means.
findings.impact: Users see raw comparison result strings like 'performance_regression' without explanation of what action to take. The meaning of result levels is not documented in the UI.
findings.fix: Map benchmark results to descriptive labels with explanations (e.g., 'PASS - Performance within tolerance', 'REGRESSION - Slower than baseline', 'FAIL - Determinism check failed'). Use a sub-box with details on what changed.
